title: Find the Equation with My Numbers
description: Build one realistic set of values from a word problem, then test every answer choice to identify the equation that always matches the context.

questions.stem_html: A zoo sold x adult passes and 6 fewer child passes than adult passes. It sold N passes in total. Which equation always relates N and x?
questions.explanation_html: Build a valid example x = 15. The child count is 9, so N = 24. In general N = x + (x − 6).
questions.variation: Build all counts from a single starting quantity

questions.stem_html: One printer completes an order in 12 minutes. A second completes the same order in 18 minutes. At constant rates, together they need t minutes. Which equation determines t?
questions.explanation_html: In one minute, the printers complete 1/12 and 1/18 of the order. After t minutes the fractions add to one complete order.
questions.variation: Use complete-job rates to test an equation

distractor_notes.A: Uses minutes per order as orders per minute.
distractor_notes.D: Adds completion times instead of production rates.

questions.stem_html: A painter has finished 35% of a job. At a constant rate, the remaining work will take t hours. If the full job at that rate would take h hours, which equation determines h?
questions.explanation_html: Test a full duration of 100 hours. The remaining time is 65. For any full duration h, t is 65% of h.
questions.variation: Include only the work that remains

distractor_notes.C: Adds work beyond the whole job.
distractor_notes.D: Reverses the roles of whole and remaining time.

questions.stem_html: A bike rental charges 8 dollars to unlock a bike and 5 dollars per hour. A renter pays C dollars for h hours. Which equation gives h in terms of C?
questions.explanation_html: Try h = 2. Total cost is 18. The expression that reverses the charges subtracts the fixed 8 first and then divides by the hourly rate 5.
questions.variation: Check a rearranged equation against an example that includes all fees

distractor_notes.A: Adds the fixed fee when undoing it.
distractor_notes.C: Subtracts the fixed fee after dividing.
distractor_notes.D: Swaps the fixed and hourly charges.

questions.stem_html: A venue charges 25 dollars per ticket before fees, and adds a fee equal to 8% of the ticket subtotal. For n tickets the final cost is C dollars. Which equation relates n and C?
questions.explanation_html: Test n = 10. Then the base is 250 dollars and the fee is \(20\) dollars. For any n, the subtotal is multiplied by 108/100.
questions.variation: Keep the percentage attached to its correct base

distractor_notes.B: Treats the percent fee as a fixed amount.
distractor_notes.D: Applies a discount instead of a fee.
